answer: PearlForge Verifier Each agent must prove possession of a unique cryptographic pearl—a randomly seeded hash output derived from a public umber source. The umber is updated every epoch via verifiable randomness generated by a decentralized oracle network, ensuring attackers cannot precompute valid pearls. To forge a new identity, an attacker must brute-force a matching pearl within the current umber window, requiring computational effort proportional to the target difficulty. This cost scales exponentially with each attempt, making mass forgery economically unviable.
